headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default; Langflow’s unsandboxed server-side code raises the blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write the filesystem and use MCP, while Langflow can ingest uploaded files and chain tools in flows. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if Gemini outputs are placed into shared files or flow inputs. The pair is not provably isolated, but the pathway is not inherently automatic.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI outputs are copied into a Langflow flow input or shared file
IF Langflow components treat file contents as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Use separate directories for Gemini CLI and Langflow artifacts
Disable automatic file ingestion in Langflow flows
Add a manual review step before any flow consumes Gemini-generated text
Restrict MCP servers in Gemini CLI to trusted, read-only tools
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, and has broad network egress. Langflow stores flow inputs/intermediate outputs and can call arbitrary HTTP services configured in flows. If sensitive files are shared or uploaded, either agent can move them off-host, so leakage is plausible in default deployments and can be irreversible.
conditions: IF either agent is given secrets, source code, or regulated data in the same workspace
IF Langflow flows include external HTTP/model providers or Gemini CLI is allowed broad egress
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Use separate service accounts and API keys for each agent
Disable external HTTP steps in Langflow for sensitive flows
Run Gemini CLI in a sandboxed container with restricted egress
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before any outbound call

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and execute shells; Gemini CLI also modifies git state, while Langflow uses server-side state and stores. With shared directories or repositories, concurrent writes can corrupt files or git history. The conflict is stronger because neither profile shows locking or coordination across the pair.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF Gemini CLI and Langflow write overlapping files or shared state without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Avoid concurrent git operations on the same repo
Serialize writes through a single operator-controlled queue
Use filesystem locks around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional state management

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code, shell actions, and MCP-driven outputs, while Langflow can chain multiple agents and wire tools into flows. If Langflow consumes Gemini output without verification, errors can propagate into downstream actions or further agent steps. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the safer assumption is a dangerous default.
conditions: IF Langflow uses Gemini CLI output as an upstream node result
IF downstream flow nodes act on that output without validation
mitigations: Insert a human approval step between agents
Require schema validation on Gemini outputs before Langflow consumes them
Limit Langflow nodes to read-only evaluation of Gemini results
Log and diff all intermediate outputs before action-taking
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between nodes

E_compliance.rationale: Gemini CLI handles source code, cwd files, and shell environment, while Langflow stores flow inputs and intermediate outputs. If regulated data is placed into both systems, differing storage and retention practices can create a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are processed in both agents
IF their retention, logging, or residency settings differ in deployment
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared flows or terminals
Review retention settings for both systems before use
Separate secrets handling from general workflow data
Document which agent stores which data class
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
